title: grpc_method_router plugin config
description: The `config` object of an enabled `grpc_method_router` plugin, generated from ferrum-edge/ferrum-edge openapi.yaml at v0.9.21 (f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3), component GrpcMethodRouterConfig and every component it references. Do not edit: run ci/plugin_config_schemas.py. This is Edge's own configuration schema, governed by Edge's support policy (docs/versioning.md); the plugin catalog records when Edge requires it.

GrpcMethodRouterConfig.description: Plugin: grpc_method_router — Per-method access control and rate limiting for gRPC services. Authorizes the backend-effective gRPC path after route rewrites, listen-path stripping, backend-path composition, and initial target selection, then populates grpc_service, grpc_method, and grpc_full_method metadata with that final method. Method rules are exact `package.Service/Method` paths or service-level `package.Service/*` rules (the method segment is exactly `*`; no other wildcard or pattern syntax). At least one access or rate rule is required. Unknown top-level keys are rejected by the runtime and by this schema. Rate-limit counter storage supports only local memory and Redis; database-backed counters are intentionally unsupported. Rejections use content-type application/grpc and map to native gRPC status from the HTTP status: 403 is PERMISSION_DENIED (denied, not allowed, or an unparseable backend-effective path), 429 is RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, and 503 is UNAVAILABLE (fail_closed Redis outage, with no rate-limit headers). A quota 429 carries x-grpc-ratelimit-limit (the matched rule's max_requests), x-grpc-ratelimit-remaining (0), and x-grpc-ratelimit-method (the refused method, without the leading slash) as initial metadata of the trailers-only response; the state-capacity 429 (a previously unseen caller key while the local map is full) carries none of them. No retry hint is sent.

allow_methods.description: Only these gRPC methods are permitted (allowlist). Each entry is a full method path like /package.Service/Method, or /package.Service/* to permit every method of one service. Leading/trailing whitespace and one optional leading slash are normalized by the runtime. Duplicate normalized forms are rejected at runtime; JSON Schema uniqueItems can reject only byte-identical duplicates. `null` is the same as omission. An empty array is valid block-all policy.

deny_methods.description: These gRPC methods are explicitly blocked; /package.Service/* blocks every method of one service. Deny takes precedence over allow, including an exact allow entry under a denied service. Duplicate normalized forms are rejected at runtime; JSON Schema uniqueItems can reject only byte-identical duplicates. `null` is the same as omission (no deny rules).

method_rate_limits.description: Per-method rate limits keyed by full method path (e.g., /myapp.UserService/CreateUser) or by a service-level /package.Service/* rule. An exact key wins over the service-level rule for that method, and only the most specific rule is charged. An exact key is a per-method budget; a service-level key is one budget per caller pooled across every method of the service that has no exact key. Duplicate normalized keys cannot be expressed by JSON Schema and are rejected at runtime. `null` is the same as omission (no per-method rates).

default_rate_limit.description: Rate limit for every method that no exact or service-level method_rate_limits key covers. It is one budget per caller pooled across all of those methods, so request-chosen method names never create new counters. Keyed by limit_by like every other rule. On its own it is a configured rule. `null` is the same as omission (uncovered methods are not rate limited).

limit_by.description: Rate limit key. Canonical values are `ip` and `consumer`; ASCII case is ignored (`CONSUMER` and `Ip` are admitted). `null` is the same as omission (`ip`). When consumer, uses identified_consumer then authenticated_identity then client IP as fallback.

sync_mode.description: gRPC method rate-limit counter storage: 'local' (in-memory) or 'redis' (centralized). ASCII case is ignored. Database-backed counters are unsupported.

redis_url.description: Redis connection URL. Required when sync_mode is 'redis'. Must not carry a URL fragment; TLS skip-verify is only FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY.

redis_tls.description: Enable TLS for the Redis connection. CA verification uses gateway-level FERRUM_TLS_CA_BUNDLE_PATH; skip-verify uses FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY.

redis_key_prefix.description: Key prefix for all Redis keys. Defaults to `{FERRUM_NAMESPACE}:{plugin_name}:{plugin-config-id}` so two independent policies of this plugin type in one namespace do not share counters. Setting this explicitly is the documented opt-in for a deliberately shared budget: every instance configured with the same prefix increments and rejects against the same counters.

redis_pool_size.description: Number of multiplexed Redis connections. Must be between 1 and 128.

redis_failure_policy.description: Behavior when the centralized Redis store cannot be consulted: an outage, an egress/DNS screen failure, or an endpoint rejected as an unsupported topology (Redis Cluster is not supported). fail_closed refuses the request with 503 and no rate-limit headers; local_fallback explicitly opts into per-process budgets, which enforce the configured limit once per gateway process. Only meaningful with sync_mode=redis, but validated in either mode.

redis_connect_timeout_seconds.description: Effective Redis connection-attempt timeout in seconds (must be ≥ 1). Applied to the redis-rs inner connection config for cached, dedicated, and health-check paths (TCP connect, TLS handshake when enabled, Redis protocol handshake). Gateway DNS screening/resolution of the Redis hostname runs before this timeout starts.

redis_health_check_interval_seconds.description: Health check ping interval when Redis is unavailable

RateSpec.description: Closed rate limit specification used by grpc_method_router (method_rate_limits entries and default_rate_limit). Both fields are required and must be positive integers; unknown keys are rejected by the runtime and by this schema.

max_requests.description: Maximum requests allowed in the window. Capped at 1000000 as an operational budget ceiling. Local sliding-window memory is bounded independently by a fixed aggregate-bucket ring per key.

window_seconds.description: Time window in seconds. Capped at 2678400 (31 days) so the window stays representable as a monotonic duration and a signed Redis TTL.
